title: Why Do Plants Make Rubber? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Aarav's mother added turmeric to the dal and it turned bright yellow, and his rubber band came from the milky sap of a rubber tree. Aarav asks: plants make colours, scents and rubber, but do they need them to stay alive? Scientists sort the chemicals of life into primary and secondary metabolites.

You will see what a metabolite is and what chemists do with one, then a zoom ladder from an animal tissue to its primary metabolites (sugars, amino acids, fatty acids, nucleotides) and a plant cell full of extra secondary metabolites. Follow curcumin from the turmeric plant to a drug, step by step, then the eight groups of secondary metabolites from the NCERT table, primary vs secondary side by side, a pause and think, six compounds sorted, the useless exam trap, an original match-the-following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 69 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
